extract: Shares of information technology firm Tata Consultancy Services rose on Friday on accelerating AI-related revenue and growth in its international business.
TCS shares were up 5.2 per cent at ₹2,183.90.

India’s $315-billion software services sector is positioning itself to benefit from the rapid adoption of artificial intelligence as global enterprises expand spending on AI-led transformation initiatives.

TCS Q2 Results: IT services giant Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) saw its share price climb almost 5% on Friday, October 9, after reporting a 15% year-on-year (YoY) increase in consolidated net profit for the July-September quarter of FY27.
The company posted a net profit of ₹13,884 crore, up from ₹12,075 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.
The company's board also announced a second interim dividend of ₹12 per share for the financial year 2026-27.

The same stood at Rs 12,075 crore a year ago.

The TCS share price is the star in trade today, up 5% intra-day.

MUMBAI: HDFC Bank's incoming MD and CEO Anup Bagchi will get target annual compensation of Rs 35.9 crore, with a Rs 7.3-crore one-time equity grant taking potential pay to Rs 43.2 crore.
He takes charge Oct 27 after Sashidhar Jagdishan's exit.

Cigarette tax hikes, inflation and rising oil prices weighed on performance.
Investors now await quarterly earnings, while brokerages remain divided on the stocks outlook and valuation prospects.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) stock may face pressure on Friday, October 9, following the US governments decision to suspend several major IT companies from its Permanent Labor Certification Program (PERM).
The development comes alongside mixed brokerage assessments of TCS Q2 FY27 results, with analysts divided over its growth prospects, operating margins and valuations.
While Nomura sees nearly 27 percent upside in TCS stock, Citi expects a further 11.4 percent downside.

Margins narrowed to 24% as hiring and operating costs increased.

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), India's largest IT services company, on Thursday reported a 15 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 13,884 crore for the September quarter, aided by broad-based growth across international markets and strong demand for
The Tata group company had posted a net profit of Rs 12,075 crore in the year-ago period and Rs 13,349 crore in the preceding June quarter.
Revenue from operations rose 11.22 per cent year-on-year to Rs 73,188 crore during the July-September quarter from Rs 65,799 crore a year ago.
Tata Group bellwether Tata Consultancy Services Ltd. reported results for the September quarter after market hours on Thursday, October 8, which were in-line to marginally below analyst expectations.

TCS reported constant currency revenue growth of 0.5%, while the CNBC-TV18 poll had projected the figure to be 0.6%.For the September quarter, TCS reported a net profit of ₹13,884 crore, compared to ₹13,349 crore during the June quarter.
The comparable figure though for the base quarter, is ₹13,849 crore as it included a one-time exceptional item of ₹668 crore due to settlement of a legal claim.
Shares of FMCG major ITC Ltd plunged 4.58 per cent in Thursday's trade to hit a 52-week low of Rs 4.57.
The decline came amid a large block deal involving 36,66,95,297 ITC shares at an average price of Rs 257.35.
The transaction was valued at Rs 9,436.90 crore.

Prabhudas Lilladher's research report on Tata Consultancy Services TCS reported 0.5% QoQ CC rev. growth, largely in line with our est. of 0.4% and consensus est. of 0.6%, with international business growing 1.2% QoQ CC.

Growth was broad-based, led by BFSI (+2.5% QoQ CC), Manufacturing (+3.1%) and Technology & Services (+3.1%), although the demand environment remained unchanged, with discretionary programs still under scrutiny and see delayed ramp ups.
Consumer and ERU segments continued to decline in Q2, but management expects Consumer to recover in Q3, supported by seasonality, while recovery in ERU is expected to be gradual.

extract: The company’s shares surged nearly 6% on Friday as investors backed its strategy to prioritize market share and AI deal pipelines over operating margins.

TCS dividend explainer: Tata Consultancy Services Limited shares surged nearly 4% during Friday’s trading session, a day after the announcement of its second quarter result for the financial year 2026-27.
The IT heavyweight has also announced its second interim dividend for FY27.
While TCS share price has seen steep decline in 2026 so far, its dividend payout remained consistent, something which is a top priority for dividend hunters.

Shares of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) were trading sharply higher on Friday, rising over 4 per cent on the National Stock Exchange after the country’s largest IT firm reported its second-quarter results on Thursday.
As of 12.21 PM, the stock was at ₹2,161, up ₹85 or 4.09 per cent from its previous close of ₹2,076, after touching an intraday high of ₹2,204.
Traded volume stood at 81.04 lakh shares worth ₹1,758 crore, reflecting heavy institutional and retail activity.
TCS’s in-line Q2 and reports of lower-than-indicated OpenAI revenue helped lift IT stocks, but muted demand, H2 margin pressure and AI-led pricing risks cloud the outlook.

Shares of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Infosys, Wipro and Coforge among others led a rebound in Indian IT stocks on Friday, helping benchmark indices recover after a sharp selloff in the previous session.

The Nifty IT index rose 3.3 percent after declining for four consecutive sessions, as investors focused on TCS' September quarter results, brushing aside concerns over the US government's reported move to suspend several Indian IT companies from the PERM programme.
All the 10 constituents of the index were trading in the green.

The Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) has partly allowed ICICI Bank’s review plea and set aside a portion of its earlier order in the case involving former ICICI Bank MD and CEO Chanda Kochhar over loans to the Videocon Group.
ICICI Bank, in its review plea, argued that it was not a party to the original proceedings and was an aggrieved party whose interests were affected by the order.
Kochhar’s counsel argued that ICICI Bank’s review application was not maintainable as the bank was not an ‘aggrieved person’.
Mumbai: Dr Reddy’s Laboratories’ said that its Andhra Pradesh based formulations manufacturing plant has received a form 483 with two observations from the US Food and Drugs Administration.

In an intimation to the stock exchanges, the company said the, Formulations Technical Operations (FTO) - 11 underwent a Pre-Approval Inspection (PAI) from October 5 to 7.“We have been issued a Form 483 with two observations, which we will address
Market response to the inspection remained muted, with Dr Reddy’s shares trading 1 per cent higher at Rs 1,195 apiece on the NSE at noon.
Anand Rathis research report on Tata Consultancy ServicesTCS delivered an encouraging Q2FY27 performance beneath a modest +0.5% q/q and +2.8% y/y CC growth.

International revenue accelerated to +1.2% q/q CC, supported by the UK (+3.5%), BFSI (+2.5%), and Manufacturing and Technology (+3.1% each), however, a sharp 10.3% decline in India following project deferrals.
North America (+0.4%) remained subdued, while Consumer (-0.7%) remains exposed to selective discretionary spend.
Mahindra is expected to unveil a new variant of the XUV 3XO in India on 15 October, with a possible factory-fitted CNG powertrain.
The automaker recently released a teaser to stir speculation about the model, but it has yet to confirm the CNG version, according to Mahindra's official press release.
If launched, the Mahindra XUV 3XO CNG would enhance the SUV's powertrain options and appeal to those seeking to cut fuel costs.
